match.reason: The bank point covers why new interwar democracies weakened, but it does not define liberal democracy as the new point does (elected representatives, rights, rule of law, several parties), so it is related rather than the same idea.

draft.title: Liberal democracy
card: In a liberal democracy, citizens vote in free elections for representatives who make the laws and form the government.
Individual rights are protected, such as free speech, a free press and freedom to meet and to worship.
The rule of law means everyone, including the government, must obey the law. Independent courts decide cases. Several parties compete, so voters have a real choice.
In the interwar years, war debts, unemployment and the Great Depression put these systems under strain. Some voters lost faith and turned to extreme movements.
draft.remember: Liberal democracy combines elected government with rights, law and choice, and hard times tested it.

a.q: Which feature best shows the rule of law in a liberal democracy?
opts: Independent courts can rule against the government
Voters choose between several parties at elections
Newspapers can print criticism of the government
Citizens are free to worship as they choose
a.why: The rule of law means the government must obey the law too, and independent courts can enforce this. Party choice, a free press and freedom of worship are also features of liberal democracy, but they belong to elections and rights.
a.clue: Think about who must obey the law.

b.q: In 1931, a country's voters face mass unemployment. Many say they no longer trust elected leaders. Which statement best explains why liberal democracy was under strain?
opts: Hardship made some voters doubt it could solve problems
Its courts had been placed under the control of one party
Its citizens had lost the right to vote in elections
Its parliament had been replaced by a single ruling party
b.why: The Depression led some voters to doubt that elected governments could fix their problems. The other options describe a country that has already stopped being a liberal democracy, not the strain on one that still is.
b.clue: The strain came from hardship, not from rights being removed.

a.best: Independent courts can rule against the government

b.best: Hardship made some voters doubt it could solve problems

problems.detail: The clue ('The strain came from hardship, not from rights being removed') all but states the answer. It points straight to the only option that mentions hardship and rules out the other three, so a student can answer without understanding the idea.
